method: Manual semantic triage by requirement family: scope ownership, safe delivery phase and evidence boundaries. This does not make a requirement accepted, complete or fully implemented.

ranges.reason: SOC console experience belongs to CyberGuard. Current preview implements only a local evidence UI subset.
restrictions: No claim that all specified modules or full accessibility acceptance are complete.

ranges.reason: Network discovery and topology remain NCC-owned; CyberGuard will consume approved read-only security context.
restrictions: No autonomous discovery, scanning or 20,000-device capacity claim in the current local preview.

ranges.reason: Endpoint telemetry and inventory are CyberGuard connector scope.
restrictions: Only a read-only local inventory and synthetic Windows event parser exist; no live agent or vulnerability inventory.

ranges.reason: Identity evidence and remote-access correlation belong to CyberGuard; temporary privileged access requires its own approved integration.
restrictions: No AD/LDAP/Entra connector, MFA-state discovery or JIT privilege executor exists.

ranges.reason: CyberGuard consumes normalized security telemetry while NCC retains network configuration control.
restrictions: No Syslog/Flow listener, firewall analyzer, NAC/NDR connector or device action exists.

ranges.reason: Authorized defensive validation and vulnerability prioritization belong to CyberGuard.
restrictions: No scanner, KEV feed, exploitation validation or production-impacting test is implemented.

ranges.reason: The safety/approval workflow belongs to CyberGuard; device and network executors require scoped integration.
restrictions: Only local asset-criticality preview/approval/rollback is implemented; no block, quarantine, service stop or switch-port action.

ranges.reason: AI interpretation and evidence timelines are CyberGuard capabilities, governed by a typed policy gateway.
restrictions: No LLM, cloud egress, evidence graph or attack-path engine is implemented.

ranges.reason: Vendor capability contracts and read/write separation are integration concerns; NCC remains the control plane for network changes.
restrictions: No Cisco, Huawei or multi-vendor connector credentials/API calls are present.

ranges.reason: Cloud security evidence belongs to CyberGuard under least-privilege integrations.
restrictions: No cloud connector, cloud credential, external telemetry or provider-specific claim is implemented.

ranges.reason: Local platform access, health, secrets and audit are CyberGuard foundations.
restrictions: Current subset is loopback RBAC/session/CSRF, source token hashing and local audit only; HTTPS, SSO/MFA, ABAC and encrypted secret vault remain pending.

ranges.reason: Quality measurement, staged validation and scaling decisions remain core platform governance.
restrictions: Score/MTTD/MTTR/multi-tenant/queue requirements are not complete; CG-063 historical no-code direction is superseded by the V3 execution decision but preserved verbatim.

ranges.reason: Versioned threat knowledge and human-reviewed detection content are CyberGuard detection engineering.
restrictions: No external knowledge feed, signature workflow or remediation recommender is implemented.

ranges.reason: Security outcomes, threat models, visibility and risk evidence are CyberGuard governance.
restrictions: Current source health is only a small visibility subset; no enterprise risk, ownership or authorized external attack-surface workflow exists.

ranges.reason: Legacy-system compatibility and continuity evidence are CyberGuard resilience scope.
restrictions: No legacy platform connector, recovery orchestration or backup validation is implemented.

ranges.reason: Privileged identity, trust and account lifecycle controls belong to CyberGuard identity integrations.
restrictions: No live directory, PAM, conditional access or credential-rotation executor exists.

ranges.reason: Endpoint protection evidence and ransomware controls are CyberGuard endpoint scope.
restrictions: No AV/EDR engine, endpoint agent, quarantine action or prevention validation is implemented.

ranges.reason: Security monitoring consumes network/OT context; network control belongs to NCC and OT changes require separate authority.
restrictions: No OT/ICS, DNS/DHCP, NAC or switch control connector exists.

ranges.reason: Cloud, application and supply-chain security evidence belong to CyberGuard.
restrictions: No SaaS, container, CI/CD or software-supply-chain connector exists.

ranges.reason: Detection quality, investigations and measurable evidence belong to CyberGuard.
restrictions: Current rules are local and deterministic; no broad detection content lifecycle or analyst quality measurement is complete.

ranges.reason: Safe response and AI policy are CyberGuard capabilities with explicit approval boundaries.
restrictions: No external response executor, AI agent or automated containment action is implemented.

ranges.reason: Saudi governance and enterprise product requirements apply to CyberGuard delivery.
restrictions: No legal, compliance, residency or procurement compliance claim is made.

ranges.reason: Network change safety depends on NCC topology/configuration data and approval workflow.
restrictions: CyberGuard has no port/VLAN/ACL execution or full network inventory.

ranges.reason: Attack-model and detection-efficacy analysis belongs to CyberGuard.
restrictions: No ATT&CK model, adversary emulation or detection-gap test harness is implemented.

ranges.reason: Identity, SaaS access and privilege review are CyberGuard connector scope.
restrictions: No SaaS/IdP collection or identity action executor is implemented.

ranges.reason: Cloud, web application and backup security evidence belong to CyberGuard.
restrictions: No cloud workload, web scanner or recovery orchestration implementation exists.

restrictions: Current contract handles structured local ingestion only; no distributed queue, OCSF adapter or multi-collector reliability proof.

ranges.reason: Safety constraints for response belong to CyberGuard policy; device/network actions require approved external executors.
